units.text: It reads and writes PowerPoint presentations in formats including .pptx, .pptm, .ppsx, .ppsm, .potx, .potm, .fodp, .gif, .html, .html5, .md, .odp, .otp, .pdf, .pot, .pps, .ppt, .swf, .tiff, .xml, and .xps. It supports creating, reading, and editing presentations, including comment authors, comments, replies, and document properties.
It creates new presentations with the default constructor or loads existing ones from a file path, then saves them to .pptx, .pptm, .ppsx, .ppsm, .potx, or .potm formats using the save method.

It manages slides through the SlideCollection interface, adding empty slides, removing slides, and cloning slides, while inserting AutoShapes, Tables, Connectors, and PictureFrames onto a slide via its ShapeCollection.

It formats text at the character, paragraph, and text-frame level through TextFrame, Paragraph, and Portion objects, applying bold, italic, underline, font size, highlight color, alignment, spacing, indentation, margins, bulleting, and text-frame wrapping and columns.

It adds speaker notes per slide through NotesSlideManager and inserts comments with authors, timestamps, and positions via CommentAuthorCollection and CommentCollection, supporting reply comments linked via set_parent_comment.

It embeds images from in-memory byte buffers via ImageCollection and manages core, application, and custom document properties such as title, author, and typed custom values through DocumentProperties.
It exports presentations to .pptx, .pptm, .ppsx, .ppsm, .potx, and .potm formats using the save method with the appropriate SaveFormat value.
It preserves unknown XML parts encountered on load by storing them verbatim and writing them back on save, ensuring round-trip fidelity for content this library does not yet understand.
It integrates with CMake projects using a minimum version of 3.20 and C++20, depending on the pugixml and miniz libraries.
Example 008 creates a new presentation, adds a comment author and two comments with a reply relationship, and saves the result as comments.pptx.
Example 009 creates a new presentation, sets built-in and custom document properties, and saves the result as deck.pptx.

Aspose.Slides FOSS for Cpp provides the Aspose.Slides FOSS for Cpp class as its primary entry point, which exposes core presentation functionality through the Presentation class. The Presentation class owns a SlideCollection of Slide objects, and each Slide exposes its shapes through ShapeCollection and its per-slide notes through NotesSlideManager.

The Aspose.Slides FOSS for Cpp class serves as the main namespace and entry point for the Aspose.Slides FOSS for Cpp library, providing access to presentation creation, manipulation, and export capabilities.

Aspose.Slides FOSS for Cpp reads and writes six Office Open XML presentation formats — Pptx, Pptm, Ppsx, Ppsm, Potx, and Potm — sharing one package layout that differs only in the content type of the main presentation part; the three macro-enabled ones are written without a VBA project, since macros aren't supported. It supports auto shapes, tables, text frames, and basic formatting, and preserves unknown XML parts encountered during load.
Charts, SmartArt, OLE objects, and mathematical text are not in the public API.
Animations and slide transitions, group shapes, hyperlinks and action settings, slide backgrounds and themes, and slide size are not supported.
Saving to a stream, adding an image from a path or a stream, and export to non-PPTX-family formats, VBA macros, and digital signatures are not supported.
Every SaveFormat value other than Pptx, Pptm, Ppsx, Ppsm, Potx, and Potm throws an error.
